title: The Bosphorus Brief — August 8, 2026
overview: A defense pact between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan dominates the region's headlines, framed by Ankara as consistent with NATO commitments. Closer to home, there's genuinely good news for international students: YÖK has confirmed an extended residence permit pathway for foreign graduates. Meanwhile, Turkey's Constitutional Court issued two notable rulings on civil liberties, and the lira remains under mild pressure ahead of expected rate cuts.
sections: <parameter name="heading">Defense Pact: What It Means Beyond the Headlines
body: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan signed a mutual defense agreement this week, with Pakistani officials describing it as a mutual-defense clause — an attack on one treated as an attack on all. Coverage is broad but framing differs: some outlets (including Haber 7) reported friction over whether the pact conflicts with NATO obligations, while Turkish officials and Middle East Eye state it aligns with, rather than replaces, NATO commitments. For residents, this is a diplomatic and defense-policy story rather than one with immediate day-to-day implications — no travel or security changes have followed from it so far.
